strings.intro: Analucia onboarding: three short moments. I only ask what changes how the project runs. If you are not sure, type unknown and the safest value is used.
strings.moment.1: Moment 1 of 3 — What project are you working on?
strings.moment.2: Moment 2 of 3 — How do you want to work?
strings.q.purpose: What is it for, in one line?
strings.h.purpose: Shown at the top of the resume. Required.
strings.q.in_use: Is it already used by real people?
strings.h.in_use: Answer no or yes. yes makes production work high risk.
strings.q.end_user_input: Do its users send text that reaches an AI model?
strings.h.end_user_input: Answer no, yes or unsure. yes or unsure: orders touching that flow are high risk and need an injection test.
strings.q.how_verified: How do you check that it works?
strings.h.how_verified: Answer tests, page (a page to look at) or person (a person checks). It sets the default checks of new orders.
strings.q.never_leaves: Which data or files must never leave this machine?
strings.h.never_leaves: Paths or patterns, separated by commas (for example secrets/**, *.sqlite). They are denied to the agents. Press Enter for none.
strings.h.delivered_when: One sentence added to every order template.
strings.q.external_artifacts: Are there documents or code made by another AI, another person or a vendor?
strings.h.external_artifacts: List their paths, separated by commas. They are recorded as unproven (hypothesis). Press Enter for none.
strings.q.github_owner: Which GitHub account owns this repository?
strings.h.github_owner: The account name only. The push guard checks it on every push.
strings.q.cloud_sessions: Will you run sessions in the cloud while your computer is off?
strings.h.cloud_sessions: Answer no or yes. yes adds the cloud-access check.
strings.h.executor_tool: For example claude-code. It is recorded when a session declares its role.
strings.h.approve_from: Answer terminal or sheet. sheet: the owner sheet (aos ceo export / import) is your channel.
strings.h.owner_locale: Answer en, pt, zh-Hans, hi or es.
strings.h.deploy_target: Answer none or the platform name. Orders that deploy are high risk.
strings.h.domain: Shown in the resume. Press Enter for none.
strings.q.budget_monthly_usd: Monthly budget for infrastructure and AI, in USD?
strings.h.budget_monthly_usd: A number, 0 or more. Alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent inform you and never stop work.
strings.h.risk_default: Answer low, medium or high. It also selects the permission profile.
strings.notice.default: Not known: the safe value is used: {value}.
strings.notice.required: {key} is required: it has no safe default.
strings.notice.budget_unknown: Budget not known: recorded as 0, and the cost alerts stay off.
strings.notice.secret_in_artifact: {path}, line {line}, looks like a credential ({pattern}). Rotate it first, through a high-risk order. The value is not shown.
strings.prompt.current: Current: {value}. Press Enter to keep it.
strings.prompt.change: Which answers do you want to change? Type their names separated by commas, or press Enter for none.
strings.prompt.invalid: That is not a valid answer. Allowed: {allowed}.
strings.plan.title: Onboarding plan
strings.plan.not_confirmed: Nothing applied: the confirmation was not CONFIRM.
strings.check.title: Setup checks
strings.tools.next_node: Install Node.js 20 or later (nodejs.org), then run aos init --check again.
strings.tools.next_git: Install Git for your system (git-scm.com), then run aos init --check again.
strings.tools.no_claude: node {node} and {git} found, but the Claude Code CLI is not on PATH or in $HOME/.local/bin
strings.tools.next_claude: Install Claude Code (claude.com/claude-code), or add $HOME/.local/bin to PATH.
strings.repo.fail: not a git work tree with an origin remote
strings.repo.next: This is normal in a copy, for example a ZIP download: you can keep working here. To keep it on GitHub, create an empty repository named {repo} in the account {owner}, then run in this folder:{cmds}
strings.account.ok: remote user and credential user are both {owner}
strings.remote_https.next: Run in this folder (SSH needs keys that most owners do not have):{cmds}
strings.reachable.ok: git ls-remote origin answered in {ms} ms with stored credentials
strings.reachable.fail: git ls-remote origin failed or took more than 30 s (no prompt was shown)
strings.reachable.next: Sign in to GitHub as {owner} once with this command; it uses that account even when this computer keeps another GitHub sign-in:{cmds}
strings.plugin_active.ok: a session started with the plugin hooks ({ts})
strings.plugin_active.warn: no session has started with the plugin hooks yet
strings.plugin_active.next: Run in this folder, then open a new Claude Code session in exactly this folder ({root}):{cmds}
strings.branch_protection.warn: branch protection cannot be checked without a token on a private repository
strings.branch_protection.next: If your plan allows it, turn on branch protection for the main branch in the repository settings on GitHub; otherwise the control is the pre-push guard plus aos verify.
strings.branch_protection.no_remote: there is no remote yet, so branch protection cannot be checked
strings.branch_protection.next_no_remote: Add a remote first (the repo line above says how), then run the check again:{cmds}
strings.cloud_access.warn: cloud sessions need the cloud GitHub connector to reach {repo}
strings.cloud_access.next: In claude.ai, open the GitHub connector settings and grant access to {repo}; then start a cloud session and confirm that it can read and push.
strings.secrets_tracked.ok: no tracked file matches a secret pattern ({files} files scanned)
strings.secrets_tracked.fail: {count} tracked line(s) match a secret pattern: {where}
strings.secrets_tracked.next: Rotate the credential first, through a high-risk order; then remove it from the repository.
strings.env_ignored.next: Add .env and .env.* to .gitignore and keep the values in a secret store, never in the repository.
strings.adopt.title: Adoption audit
strings.adopt.read_only: Read only: nothing in the project was changed. Secret values are never shown.
strings.adopt.proposals: Proposed orders (text only: the director writes the orders after you read this report)
strings.adopt.summary: {high} high · {medium} medium · {low} low · {info} info · {nv} not verified
strings.adopt.f.secret_tree: a {kind} secret is in a tracked file
strings.adopt.f.secret_history: a {kind} secret was added in commit {commit}; it stays in the history even if the file changed or was deleted
strings.adopt.f.noncode: a non-code file (.{ext}) is inside a code folder
strings.adopt.f.migration_dup: migration prefix {prefix} is used by more than one file
strings.adopt.f.docs_missing: the document names {ref}, which does not exist in the tree
strings.adopt.f.docs_script: the document names npm run {ref}, but package.json has no such script
strings.adopt.f.backup_none: no backup or deploy script was found
strings.adopt.f.backup_stale: the newest backup output is {hours} hours old
strings.adopt.f.spof_no_remote: the repository has no remote: the code exists only on this machine
strings.adopt.f.spof_unpushed: {n} commit(s) on {branch} are not on any remote
strings.adopt.f.spof_untracked: a large source file ({kb} KB) is untracked and not ignored
strings.adopt.f.deps_lock: package.json declares dependencies but there is no lockfile
strings.adopt.n.secret: Rotate this credential first, at its provider (owner, high-risk order); then remove it from the repository.
strings.adopt.n.secret_history: Rotate this credential first (owner, high-risk order); cleaning the history is a second order, after rotating.
strings.adopt.n.env: Untrack the file (git rm --cached), add it to .gitignore, and rotate any value it held, through an order.
strings.adopt.n.hygiene: Move the file out of the repository (to an artifact store or a backup location) through a fix order.
strings.adopt.n.docs: Correct the document, or restore what it names, through a fix order.
strings.adopt.n.backup: Add a backup or deploy script with visible output, or record where it runs, through an order.
strings.adopt.n.backup_stale: Check the scheduled job: its latest output is older than 48 hours.
strings.adopt.n.spof: Push the work to a remote you control (git push), or add one.
strings.adopt.n.tests: Add a test command (for example npm test) through a fix order.
strings.adopt.n.deps: Commit a lockfile and pin the versions through a fix order.
strings.adopt.nv.branch: Branch protection is not visible from the repository (SPEC-0005).
strings.adopt.nv.backup: Backup or deploy output is not visible from the repository.
strings.adopt.nv.tests: A test command exists ({where}); it is not run, because the audit is read only.
strings.adopt.nv.ports: Ports named in documents are not checked.
strings.adopt.nv.history: The git history could not be read.
strings.adopt.p.rotate: Rotate the {kind} credential found in {file} ({where}). Risk high, owner only: the owner rotates it at the provider. The value is not written here.
strings.adopt.p.clean_history: After rotating, remove the rotated secrets from the git history: a second order, risk high, owner only.
strings.queue.title: Queue
strings.queue.intro: Every order that is not signed yet, in the order it will be done (dependencies first, then id).
strings.queue.empty: Nothing in the queue: every order is signed.
strings.sign.none: Nothing to sign: no order is finished or checked.
strings.sign.ready: {id} passed its checks and can be signed.
strings.sign.failed: {id} did not pass ({why}); it stays open.
strings.sign.already: {id} was already checked and can be signed.
strings.sign.nothing_passed: No order passed its checks, so there is nothing to sign.
strings.sign.not_confirmed: Nothing was signed: the confirmation was not CLOSE.
strings.sign.no_git: This folder is not a git repository: the sign-off is recorded in the log only.
strings.q.hosting: Where will the project be hosted?
strings.h.hosting: Answer managed (a platform runs it for you), own-server (a server you rent), already: <where it runs>, or later. later is always valid; change it with aos init --hosting.
strings.hosting.title: Hosting options (approximate monthly cost, sorted by cost)
strings.hosting.columns: option | kind | USD per month | operated by | recovery after a failure | who holds the keys | checked on | source
strings.hosting.recovery.managed: the platform restarts the service; the owner redeploys from git
strings.hosting.recovery.own-server: as fast as the owner restores the last tested backup
strings.hosting.keys.managed: the platform runs the servers; the owner holds the account and the app secrets
strings.hosting.keys.own-server: the owner holds every key: server, account and app secrets
strings.hosting.stale: checked {days} days ago: this price may be out of date.
strings.hosting.prices_change: Prices change: check the source before you decide.
strings.hosting.checklist_note: This checklist is text: Analucia never touches any server.
strings.review.choose: Type approve, comment or reject (or open to see it; Enter = decide later):
strings.review.open_failed: It could not be opened; the file is {path}.
strings.review.invalid: Type approve, comment, reject or open.
strings.review.done.comment: Comment recorded: the agent will see it.
strings.review.done.reject: Rejected: the agent will see the reason.
strings.admit.open_hint: If this is a correction or an extension of one of these, write an addendum to it instead of a new order.
strings.backup.saved: Saved {files} files, including work not committed yet, to the branch {branch} on {remote}. To bring it back: aos backup --restore-hint
strings.backup.refused: Nothing was saved: {n} place(s) look like a secret. The files are listed below; the values are not shown.
strings.backup.hint_title: The latest backup is {branch} on {remote}. To restore it in a new folder next to this one, without touching your current work:
strings.backup.hint_none: There is no backup on {remote} yet: run aos backup.
strings.repo.next_no_owner: This is normal in a copy, for example a ZIP download: you can keep working here. To keep it on GitHub, first name the GitHub account that owns the project:{cmds}
strings.account.next_no_owner: Name the GitHub account that owns the project:{cmds}
strings.check.later: not checked yet: the project has no remote (origin)
strings.check.next_later: Nothing to do now: this check runs again once the remote exists.
strings.check.no_github: not used: the owner works without GitHub
strings.check.next_no_github: Nothing to do: the work stays on this computer, so keep your own backup copy of this folder.
strings.plugin_active.next_here: The plugin is installed for this folder. Open a new Claude Code session in exactly this folder ({root}), not in a subfolder: Claude Code loads a project plugin only in the folder it was installed for.
strings.plugin_active.next_elsewhere: The plugin is installed for another folder ({count} in all), not for this one, and Claude Code loads it only there. Run in this folder, then open a new session in exactly this folder ({root}):{cmds}
strings.session.not_initialised: Analucia AOS is installed, but this folder is not initialised: no .analucia folder in {cwd} or above it. To start, run this in your own terminal, in this folder: {cmd}
strings.session.root_sub: Project root: {root} (this session started in the subfolder {cwd})
strings.w.title: Setting up Analucia AOS for this project: 15 questions in 3 blocks of 5. It takes about 5 minutes, and nothing is changed until you approve the plan at the end.
strings.w.howto: Type the number of your answer and press Enter. Type 0 to go back. Press Enter alone to keep the current answer.
strings.w.question: Question {n} of {total}
strings.w.invalid: Type a number from 1 to {max}, or 0 to go back.
strings.w.invalid_typed: That answer cannot be used. An account name has only letters, numbers and dashes.
strings.w.first: This is the first question; there is nothing to go back to.
strings.w.type_place: Say where in a few words:
strings.w.summary_change: Type a question number (1 to 15) to change that answer, or press Enter to see the plan.
strings.w.q.1: Can people outside your team type or upload things into the project (forms, files, comments)?
strings.w.q.2: Which private information does the project keep?
strings.w.o.2.2: Personal details of customers (names, phones, addresses)
strings.w.o.2.5: Not sure: treat everything as private
strings.w.q.3: How careful must the assistant be before it changes something?
strings.w.o.3.1: Very careful: it asks you more often
strings.w.o.3.3: Light: it asks you only for big steps
strings.w.q.4: Where do you want to approve finished work?
strings.w.o.4.1: In a spreadsheet I fill in
strings.w.q.5: Which GitHub account owns this project?
strings.w.o.5.2: Another account: I will type its name
strings.w.o.6.2: An app people use (web or phone)
strings.w.o.6.3: An internal tool for my team
strings.w.q.8: How do you check that a change works?
strings.w.q.9: How many tasks may the assistant work on at the same time?
strings.w.o.10.1: When the checks pass and I looked at it
strings.w.q.11: Which language should Analucia use with you?
strings.w.q.12: Where will the project run for the people who use it?
strings.w.o.12.2: A service that runs it for me
strings.w.o.12.4: It already runs somewhere (I will say where)
strings.w.q.13: Is there a live version that must not break?
strings.w.o.13.2: Yes: saving to the main branch updates it
strings.w.o.13.3: Yes: someone publishes it by hand
strings.w.q.14: Should the assistant also work when your computer is off (in the cloud)?
strings.w.q.15: How much can you spend per month on AI and hosting?
